title: gpt-oss: OpenAI's Open-Weight Models
hook: OpenAI's first open-weight release since GPT-2: two Apache-2.0 reasoning models, the larger running on a single 80GB GPU and the smaller on a 16GB laptop.
key_points: gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, released August 2025 under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
OpenAI's first open-weight language models since GPT-2 in 2019.
Mixture-of-Experts reasoning models — only a fraction of parameters fire per token.
120b runs on one 80GB GPU; 20b runs on edge devices with ~16GB of memory.
content_html: In August 2025, OpenAI released gpt-oss — two open-weight models, gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b — under the permissive Apache 2.0 license. It was the company's first open-weight release since GPT-2 in 2019, a notable reversal for a lab whose name had become synonymous with closed frontier models.
extra_html:
What's new

Both models are Mixture-of-Experts reasoning models, activating only a small fraction of their parameters per token for efficiency. The larger gpt-oss-120b is designed to run on a single 80GB GPU, while gpt-oss-20b fits on edge devices with around 16GB of memory, making strong local inference practical. OpenAI reported the models trade blows with its smaller hosted reasoning models on coding, math, and tool-use benchmarks.

Why it matters

Open weights mean anyone can download, fine-tune, and run the models privately, without sending data to an API. After years of pressure from the open-weight ecosystem — Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek — OpenAI re-entering it with a permissive license was a significant signal about where competitive pressure was pushing the field. The Apache 2.0 license in particular allows unrestricted commercial use.

related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.

flashcards.prompt: Why does the Mixture-of-Experts design let gpt-oss-20b run on a 16GB device?
flashcards.back_html: Only a small fraction of parameters fire per token, so the per-token compute and memory stay low enough for edge hardware.
